title: Understanding Curriculum Learning in Large Language Models via Cross-Difficulty Optimization Dynamics
abstract: arXiv:2608.17268v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Curriculum learning has been widely adopted in the post-training of large language models by organizing training data from easy to hard. However, its effectiveness varies substantially across reasoning tasks, suggesting that no single curriculum is universally optimal and raising a fundamental question: what determines when curriculum learning works? In this paper, we answer this question by analyzing the optimization dynamics induced by different curriculum schedules. translated_title: 通过跨难度优化动态理解大型语言模型中的课程学习
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.17268v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：课程学习通过将训练数据从易到难组织，已广泛应用于大型语言模型的后训练中。然而，其效果在不同推理任务间差异显著，这表明没有单一的课程是普遍最优的，并引发了一个基本问题：什么决定了课程学习何时有效？在本文中，我们通过分析不同课程计划所引发的优化动态来回答这个问题。我们表明，不同难度水平之间的迁移关系刻画了课程学习引发的优化动态，这反过来解释了不同课程计划的有效性，并将这种关系形式化为“相对迁移”（Relative Transfer），这是一种跨难度知识迁移的原则性度量。基于这一度量，我们推导出迁移感知的动态课程采样（TDCS），它动态调整采样分布。
tldr: 本文通过提出“相对迁移”度量，揭示了课程学习有效性的关键决定因素，并据此设计出动态调整采样分布的TDCS方法，以提升大型语言模型在不同推理任务中的训练效果。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces "Relative Transfer" as a principled measure to explain when curriculum learning works in LLMs, and proposes Transfer-aware Dynamic Curriculum Sampling (TDCS) to dynamically adjust sampling distributions for improved training across reasoning tasks.
